post.description:
List action items with optional filters and pagination.
Privileged access allows you to get action items for the account.
Non-privileged access allows you to get action items for the authenticated user only.

The `scope` filter controls which action items are returned:
- (no scope - default): All action items the user has access to
- assigned_to_me: Only action items assigned to the authenticated user
- assigned_to_others: Only action items the user can edit, assigned to teammates

The `created_at_start`, `created_at_end`, `updated_at_start` and `updated_at_end` filters take a
YYYY-MM-DD date or an ISO datetime and are inclusive. A value without a time means midnight UTC, so
pass a time on an end bound (`2024-01-05T23:59:59`) to cover the whole day. To page through a window
of changes, combine `updated_at_start` with `order_by: updated_at_asc`.

Whether `updated_at` moves depends on where the change was made. Edits in the note itself, including
its text, completion, assignees and due date, all bump `updated_at`. An assignee or due date changed
outside the note, such as from the action items list, is written to a separate record and leaves
`updated_at` unchanged, so the `updated_at` filters do not pick that item up.

A value without a time means midnight UTC, so an end bound of 2024-01-05 excludes everything later that day. Whether updated_at moves depends on where the change was made. Edits in the note itself, including its text, completion, assignees and due date, all bump updated_at. An assignee or due date changed outside the note, such as from the action items list, is written to a separate record and leaves updated_at unchanged, so this filter does not pick that item up.
updated_at_start.title: Updated At Start

updated_at_end.description: Only return action items updated at or before this date. Accepts YYYY-MM-DD or an ISO datetime, and is inclusive. A value without a time means midnight UTC, so an end bound of 2024-01-05 excludes everything later that day. Whether updated_at moves depends on where the change was made. Edits in the note itself, including its text, completion, assignees and due date, all bump updated_at. An assignee or due date changed outside the note, such as from the action items list, is written to a separate record and leaves updated_at unchanged, so this filter does not pick that item up.
updated_at_end.title: Updated At End

post.description:
Create a new webhook endpoint.

Creates a webhook that will receive HTTP POST requests when subscribed events occur.
The webhook will be associated with the authenticated user.

Set `scope` to `workspace` to create an account-wide webhook instead, which receives every
matching event in the account and is delivered once per event rather than once per attendee.
**Super Admin Access Required** for that value: a key acting through `X-On-Behalf-Of` cannot
create one, because impersonation drops privileged access.

WebhookCreateResponse.description: Response for webhook creation, includes the secret (only returned once).
WebhookCreateResponse.title: WebhookCreateResponse

WebhookWithSecret.description: Webhook response that includes the secret, only returned on creation.
WebhookWithSecret.title: WebhookWithSecret

CreateWebhookRequest.description: Request body for creating a webhook.

url.description: The URL endpoint that will receive webhook POST requests
url.title: Url

enabled_events.description: List of event types to subscribe to. Valid values: 'ai_note.shared_to_channel', 'ai_note.generated', 'action_item.assigned', 'action_item.completed'.
enabled_events.title: Enabled Events

description.description: Optional description for this webhook endpoint
description.title: Description

scope.description: Who the webhook belongs to. 'user' is the authenticated user, the default and the existing behaviour. 'workspace' is the whole account: it receives every matching event with no per-user filter, and each event is delivered once rather than once per attendee. Creating one requires a privileged API key.
scope.title: Scope

patch.description:
Update an existing webhook endpoint.

Allows partial updates - only provided fields will be modified.
The webhook must belong to the authenticated user (or account for privileged access).

An account-wide webhook is updated through this same endpoint, and needs a privileged key:
without one its id reads as not found, the same answer as another user's webhook.

`scope` cannot be changed after creation, and is ignored here: a webhook's scope decides
which Svix application its endpoint lives in, so converting one means deleting and
recreating it.
